components.gap: Durrett defines uniform integrability for an arbitrary collection of random variables, with no integrability hypothesis (sec. 4.6, printed p. 244), and remarks that a choice of M making the supremum less than one gives sup E|X_i| <= M + 1 < infinity, so integrability of every member is a consequence of the definition. The route definition (body lines 17-22) is stated only for a family of real integrable random variables, and the M + 1 bound (annex lines 6-7) is derived only for families already assumed integrable. No route text gives the source's form for an arbitrary collection or states that the tail condition forces integrability (a non-integrable member has infinite tail mean at every level). Narrowed source variant: an added hypothesis replaces a derived consequence.

components.gap: Durrett's Theorem 4.6.2 (printed p. 245) takes phi >= 0 to be any function with phi(x)/x -> infinity and an arbitrary collection with E phi(|X_i|) <= C for all i, and concludes uniform integrability, so integrability of each X_i is part of the conclusion; he introduces it as a common way to check uniform integrability. The route entry (body lines 49-51) requires Phi to be finite and Borel measurable and applies to the family of the definition, which presupposes integrable X_i (body lines 17-18); the annex proof (lines 36-46) never derives integrability from the moment bound. No route text states the criterion without the integrability presupposition, or says that the source's expectation hypothesis is what requires phi(|X_i|) to be measurable. Narrowed source variant.

components.gap: The source's continuation of Theorem 4.6.9 (printed pp. 247-248) presents two readings of Levy's 0-1 law, introduced with a line borrowed from Chung inviting the reader to judge whether the result is obvious or incredible: the obvious reading (the best guess of 1_A given F_n should approach 1_A, the best guess given F_infinity) and the incredible reading (for independent variables and a tail event, E(1_A | F_n) = P(A) for every n, so P(A) = 1_A a.s. and P(A) is 0 or 1); it then says this and later applications show the theorem is very useful. The route supplies the theorem, its L1 strengthening and the Kolmogorov 0-1 derivation (body lines 162-174, annex lines 289-303) but not the two-readings discussion, the attribution of the line to Chung, or the usefulness claim; the body only says it supplies the source's separate conditional-limit proof of Kolmogorov's law. Omitted justificatory and historical claims.

components.gap: Source Example 4.6.11 (printed p. 248) opens with a general claim: if X_1, X_2, ... are uniformly integrable and converge a.s. to X, Theorem 4.6.3 gives L1 convergence and, combined with Exercise 4.6.7, E(X_n | F) -> E(X | F) in L1 for a fixed sigma-field F; the example then shows that a.s. convergence of E(X_n | F) can fail. The route states only the instance (body lines 209-215: E(X_n | G) = B_n tends to zero in L1) and the two ingredients separately (thm:p15-vitali-convergence, thm:p15-changing-conditional-limits (1); see also the decreasing-information boundary theorem in exchangeability-and-predictive-induction-w02b-p15-022.tex lines 926-948); the general L1 conclusion for a uniformly integrable a.s.-convergent sequence and fixed information, with its two-step justification, is not written. The construction itself is complete (annex lines 368-388).

components.gap: Source Exercise 4.6.1 (printed p. 248) gives the statistical reading of the model: with normal(0,1) Z_i the observations are a sample from a normal population with variance 1 and unknown mean; the distribution of theta is called the prior distribution, and P(theta in . | Y_1, ..., Y_n) the posterior distribution after n observations. The route entry (body lines 257-269) uses the phrases 'integrable prior variable' and 'unrestricted posterior consistency claim' but never defines the prior distribution as the law of theta, never identifies P(theta in . | F_n) as the posterior distribution after n observations or E(theta | F_n) as its mean, and gives only 'independent normal (0,1) noise' for the normal-population reading; the on-route posterior construction (def:p15-bayes-experiment) assumes a dominated experiment and is not linked. Omitted source definitions and interpretive claims.
